cards.intuition: Sorted absolute IDs may be huge, but neighboring differences are often small. Store the first ID and then those differences.
Recover absolute IDs by accumulating gaps. A restart base at each block lets a reader begin without decoding the whole list.
cards.formula: di = sum from j=1 to i of gj

cards.intuition: Frequent terms have more postings but smaller average spaces between documents, often reducing bits per posting.
cards.formula: average gap roughly N / document frequency

cards.intuition: Split an integer into seven-bit payload groups and use one marker bit per byte to show whether the integer ends.
cards.formula: base-128 payload groups + continuation or terminal bit

cards.intuition: Small values finish in one byte, while larger values add bytes only for themselves rather than widening a whole block.
It is simple and handles mixed magnitudes, but marker overhead and branchy byte loops lose to SIMD block packing on many hot streams.
cards.formula: choose from ratio + decode throughput + restart needs

cards.intuition: Postings and Parquet both transform structure into small residuals, then encode only the bits those residuals need.
cards.formula: structured values → reversible low-entropy transform → compact code

cards.intuition: Search selectively traverses and skips latency-critical lists; analytics decodes selected pages into large vectorized batches.
cards.formula: postings: selective navigation; Parquet: page scan

cards.intuition: Document order creates small postings gaps. Column order creates small deltas, long runs, and tight row-group statistics.
cards.formula: sorting → smaller residuals and faster access

cards.intuition: The smallest artifact is not automatically fastest. Optimize avoided storage and memory movement against decode CPU and navigation complexity.
cards.formula: net value = byte-movement savings - decode and complexity cost
